evaluations.answer: The logs reveal a consistent self-regulation pattern: Ahmad anchors himself to predictable, controllable sensory inputs whenever he faces uncertainty or sensory overwhelm, across settings that on the surface appear unrelated. Physical comfort objects (rocks) serve as grounding tools in anxiety-provoking situations-he brings his green rock and smooth rock to the doctor visit specifically to hold during the shot, the loss of the pool rock produces visceral distress ('my tummy feels weird. that one was my pool one'), and he plans comfort rocks before the next booster. Drawing and journaling convert overwhelming sensory experience into a controlled, self-paced output-at recess he observes an ant trail rather than playing chase and records three pages in his sketchbook; after the noisy pool he draws a turtle; he draws a raccoon after an emotionally charged day. Quiet routines and preferred music (slow piano, 'moonlight song', Beethoven) reduce environmental noise load while he works; he explicitly asks to 'sit by the fence and listen for a minute first' before a field walk. Adult explanations before events give Ahmad a cognitive map that allows him to proceed: he needs to know the 'germ part first before the pinch part,' is shown the swim schedule card the night before Tuesday, and his father frames the protest conversation explicitly on the porch. The unifying mechanism is that Ahmad manages novelty and overwhelm by creating predictability-through physical anchors, advance information, or conversion of experience into controlled observational or artistic form. What would be too strong to conclude is that Ahmad cannot engage with new situations without adult scaffolding or that he shows clinical avoidance. He self-initiates many of these strategies (packing rocks himself, choosing observation over play, asking for explanations unprompted); his drawing and nature observation show high engagement and curiosity rather than withdrawal; and he successfully completes challenging situations (the shot, the noisy pool, meeting a new classmate) when appropriate supports are in place.
